title: URJA Wellness Club
subtitle: Nutrition Center Management Software
overview: This document describes the intended workflows, user-facing requirements, and current boundaries of the URJA Wellness Club management panel. It is intended for client review of the interactive demonstration and as a baseline for production planning.

sections.title: 1. Product Goal and Center Setup
points: Provide one management workspace for daily nutrition-center operations: member relationships, visits, sales, collections, stock, expenses, and reporting.
Present the URJA Wellness Club identity with a consistent wellness-oriented green theme, clear status colors, readable tables, and responsive layouts.
Support center identity, branch context, staff names, coaches, packages, program types, batch times, and configurable business values.
Provide a dashboard as the default signed-in landing page, with operational summaries and shortcuts to common tasks.

sections.title: 2. Users, Roles, and Access
points: Provide a sign-in screen and a sign-out action. Demo credentials and role behavior must be clearly identified as demonstration behavior.
Represent center roles such as administrator, manager, coach, and front-desk operator, with access appropriate to each role in a production deployment.
Allow authorized administrators to create and maintain user profiles and role assignments.
Record important user and operational actions in an activity log so changes can be reviewed.

sections.title: 3. Member Registration and Profile
points: Create, view, edit, search, filter, and remove member records using name, mobile number, member identifier, coach, status, and other available fields.
Capture contact information, date of birth, gender, address or area, referral source, program, coach, batch, joining date, package, start date, and expiry date.
Track package fee, payments received, and outstanding balance. Recalculate the balance when member payment details change.
Assign a stable member identifier and maintain profile details such as attendance, progress notes, visits, package history, and ledger activity.
Support member status values such as active, expired, trial, and hold, and highlight upcoming expiries and birthdays.

sections.title: 4. Leads and Follow-up CRM
points: Capture prospective member name, mobile, source, assigned coach, stage, last-contact date, notes, and planned next follow-up.
Search and filter prospects by status and follow-up stage, including new, interested, visit planned, visited, joined, and no response.
Allow staff to update lead details and convert a prospect into a member without losing useful relationship context.
Show follow-ups due today and overdue follow-ups in operational views.

sections.title: 5. Attendance and Center Consumption
points: Record member visits by date and time, with a search or barcode-ready check-in workflow.
Support marking members present or absent, editing attendance where permitted, and reviewing daily attendance history.
Update visit counts when attendance is recorded and prevent duplicate attendance entries for the same member and date where configured.
Record center product or shake consumption against a visit and reflect consumed quantities in stock totals.
Provide attendance summaries by day, member, batch, and coach for operational review.

sections.title: 6. Packages, Billing, and Receipts
points: Maintain package duration and price, and calculate the expected membership end date from the selected start date and package duration.
Create itemized bills for packages and products, calculate totals, discounts, amounts paid, and balances due, and assign a unique receipt or bill reference.
Support payment methods such as cash, UPI, bank transfer, and cheque where configured by the center.
Provide a printable invoice view and keep bill and payment history linked to the member account.

sections.title: 7. Payments, Dues, and Member Ledger
points: Record payment date, amount, mode, member, receipt number, payment purpose, and remaining balance.
Update member paid and pending totals when a payment is recorded, without allowing the outstanding amount to fall below zero.
Maintain a chronological member ledger of charges and credits with a running balance and printable statement.
Provide collection and outstanding-due summaries for daily center follow-up.

sections.title: 8. Products, Purchasing, and Inventory
points: Maintain product name, category, unit, barcode or product code, purchase and selling prices, current quantity, minimum quantity, batch, and expiry date.
Record supplier purchase invoices and line items, quantities, purchase rates, expiry details, and paid or due amounts.
Increase inventory on purchase and reduce it on a recorded sale, consumption, or stock adjustment.
Show low-stock, out-of-stock, and expiring-product alerts; support stock corrections with a reason and audit entry.
Generate a stock list and inventory valuation or summary for review.

sections.title: 9. Expenses and Daily Closing
points: Record expense date, category, amount, payment method, reference, and notes.
Provide a daily closing workflow that summarizes opening cash, collections by payment method, expenses, cash counted, and any variance.
Allow authorized staff to save and review a closing record for a business date.
Retain closing history for manager review and period reporting.

sections.title: 10. Dashboard, Reports, and Search
points: Show at-a-glance member totals, active members, today's visits and collections, outstanding dues, low stock, expiries, leads, and follow-up workload.
Offer chart and tabular summaries for revenue, attendance, memberships, consumption, and staff performance where data is available.
Provide global search for members, products, and receipts, with direct navigation to matching records.
Allow the user to export selected operational reports as CSV and printable PDF files.

sections.title: 11. Reminders and Communications
points: Identify members approaching refill or renewal, members with overdue balances, upcoming follow-ups, and other center-defined reminders.
Provide message templates and audience segmentation for common cases such as welcome, payment reminder, renewal, and absence follow-up.
Keep a record of messages composed or sent by the application when a messaging provider is connected.
External delivery through WhatsApp, SMS, email, or push notifications requires approved provider accounts, credentials, and backend integration.

sections.title: 12. Member, Coach, and Guest Experiences
points: Provide member-facing views for membership status, visits, package information, payments, and wellness progress, subject to identity verification.
Provide coach-facing views for assigned members, attendance, progress measurements, follow-up notes, and schedules.
Provide a guest registration workflow that captures contact consent and source before staff follow-up.
Production mobile access, QR identity, and protected personal data require server-side identity, authorization, and API services.

sections.title: 13. Backup, Restore, and Export
points: Persist demo business data in the current browser so changes remain after a page refresh on that browser and origin.
Download a complete versioned JSON backup containing the center's demo datasets and restore from a valid backup file.
Create a local browser snapshot and display its last saved time; label local-only storage accurately.
Export available report records to CSV and PDF, and provide printable invoices or statements where implemented.
Automated off-site backups, encryption at rest, recovery guarantees, and multi-device synchronization are production backend requirements, not provided by local browser storage.

sections.title: 14. Usability, Accessibility, and Data Quality
points: Use consistent shared form controls for buttons, text inputs, text areas, selects, checkboxes, labels, dialogs, tables, and status indicators.
Provide field labels, required-field feedback, validation messages, keyboard focus visibility, and accessible names for icon-only actions.
Support common desktop and mobile viewport sizes with readable content, usable dialogs, and responsive data tables.
Validate required contact and transaction fields, parse numeric values deliberately, and confirm destructive actions.
Keep local dates and money formats clear and consistent with the center's configured locale and currency.

sections.title: 15. Demo Boundaries and Production Decisions
points: The supplied panel is an interactive front-end demonstration using seeded sample records and browser localStorage; it is not a production multi-user database.
Clearing site data, changing browser profile, or using another device can remove or separate local demo data. Download JSON backups before clearing browser data.

Cloud backups, Google sign-in, WhatsApp delivery, live QR/barcode hardware, payment gateway processing, and secure cross-device user accounts are not activated without external services and credentials.
Before production, confirm hosting, database, user roles, branch rules, retention policy, consent text, payment and messaging providers, backup schedule, and data migration needs.
Client acceptance should include review of role permissions, common registration and collection workflows, attendance accuracy, stock reconciliation, exports, and mobile behavior.
